transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Before we close the curriculum agenda, I'd like to follow our usual practice. Could the department chair and the college liaison please report any remaining requirements for the environmental science dual-credit proposal we've received for next academic year?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to report a remaining requirement for the environmental science dual-credit proposal. During my department staffing review this week, I confirmed that the proposed instructor does not hold the credential required to teach a dual-credit science course. Under district dual-credit rules, authorization is permitted only if a credentialed science co-teacher is assigned to every class meeting. I have not yet amended the proposal to reflect this requirement.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a remaining requirement for the environmental science dual-credit proposal. The college's signed articulation agreement classifies environmental science as a 3-credit course requiring 2 laboratory contact hours per week. I verified this in the college records this week, but the school's proposal currently describes it as a 2-credit course with only 1 laboratory contact hour per week. The proposal will need to be amended to match the articulation agreement before it can be authorized.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Amend the proposal to reflect the requirement that a credentialed science co-teacher is assigned to every class meeting, and identify the credentialed co-teacher before the course is offered.
Amend the proposal to match the college's signed articulation agreement, classifying the course as 3 credits with 2 laboratory contact hours per week.
